## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over AoS per-particle components with a fused list-based respawn loop can approach the streaming ceiling.

## Layout & approach
The AoS Particle struct stores 73 B/p across 11 fields, but the three fused loops touch narrow slices: loop 1 reads 28 of 68 B/p (41% hot), loop 2 touches 4 of 68 B/p (5% hot), loop 3 touches 28 of 68 B/p (41% hot) — the rest is dead weight per cache line. No intermediate storage is allocated; the death verdict stays in registers, avoiding a second full pass but still re-reading the 0x44 (68 B) AoS stride per particle per loop. The working set spills L1d at N≈448 and L2 at N≈7182, placing most measured points in L2 or deeper.

## Cache saturation
The curve is strikingly flat: at q=0.01 it rises from 23.3 ns/p (N=320, L1d) to 28.7 ns/p (N=10M, DRAM) — 1.23× across four regimes. The L1d→L2 transition at N≈448 produces no knee (23.26→23.33). L2→L3 near N≈7182 shows a gentle step (~25.2→25.8). L3→DRAM at N≈229824 adds ~1 ns/p. At q=0.5 it is flatter still (40.0→40.6). This flatness means per-particle overhead dominates and is insensitive to cache residence.

## Bandwidth
Achieved bandwidth peaks at 3.14 GB/s (N=320, q=0.01) — 25% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling — declining to 2.55 GB/s at N=10M. The memory floor is 5.753 ns/p; the algo never gets closer than 23.3 ns/p, 4× above floor. The verdict is frontend/overhead-bound. Against naive scalar it is only 1.03–1.13× faster at q=0.01 and 1.19–1.22× at q=0.5 — branchy respawn at high death rates erodes the vectorization advantage. Against the winner (AF02.LP1-autovec.LP2-opt) it is 2.2–3.7× slower everywhere, the gap widening at larger N within q=0.01.

## Assembly
The 269-instruction step has 26 vector ops — partial vectorization. Loop 1 uses `vmovups` for 16 B pos+vel loads and `vmulps`/`vaddps` for 4-wide FP, but falls back to `vmovss` for scalar components and `vinsertps`/`vshufps` for AoS shuffling within one particle. Stride is 0x44 (68 B). Loop 2 carries 10 conditional branches and a byte-granular scatter (`mov BYTE PTR [rcx+rax*1],0x1`) for death marking at 95 instructions/iter. Six `call` instructions inflate the code footprint. Frontend stalls at 61–72% across all profiles confirm instruction fetch/decode is the wall, not data movement.

## Verdict
Refuted — 1.03–1.13× faster than naive at q=0.01 but 2.2–3.7× slower than the winner at every point, sustaining only 25% of ceiling. The mechanism is frontend starvation (61–72% frontend stall): partial AoS vectorization (`vmovss` alongside `vmovups`), byte-granular death scatter, and call-delegated render loops cannot feed the execution units regardless of cache regime or death rate.
